senses.definition: Alternative letter-case form of Bible (“a specific version, edition, translation, or copy of the Christian religious text”).
senses.example: [Editor David W. Blight said:] Deeply in need of father figures and spiritual hope, and “religiously seeking knowledge,” as he recalled it, the slave boy [the young Frederick Douglass] turned to a religious black man, a freeman named Charles Lawson, who worked as a drayman for a rope maker and lived on Happy Alley in Fells Point. Frederick spent countless hours with Lawson in the drayman’s shack reading the bible aloud, singing hymns, and praying together. “I could teach him the letter, but he could teach me the spirit,” Douglass remembered. Throughout his life Douglass would teach his teachers and learn from them at the same time. From old Lawson he gained […] above all […] a belief in a benevolent and protective God, the faith that his “life was under the guidance of a wisdom higher than my own.”

senses.definition: Alternative letter-case form of Bible (“the analogous holy book of another religion”).
Alternative letter-case form of Bible (“a specific version, edition, translation, or copy of the Christian religious text”).
senses.example: If a person should happen to meet them when on these journeys, he should, if he has not a bible in his pocket, draw a circle round him on the ground, and in God's name forbid their approach.

senses.definition: Alternative letter-case form of Bible (“the analogous holy book of another religion”).
senses.example: The Buddhist bible tells this story of Buddha’s time of temptation when he was living as a hermit on the Mount of Snow.

senses.definition: A comprehensive manual that describes something, or a publication with a loyal readership; a foundational text.
A binder containing copies of the most important documents for a particular matter.
senses.example: Could you please add these to the case bible?

senses.definition: Synonym of holystone: a piece of sandstone used for scouring wooden decks on ships.
A compilation of problems and solutions from previous years of a given course, used by some students to cheat on tests or assignments.
senses.example: My friend’s a genius, he will give me problems one through nine. The bible of a sophomore will have the needed lines.

senses.definition: Omasum, the third compartment of the stomach of ruminants
The upper part of a pin-tumbler lock, containing the driver pins and springs.
Either of two major versions of the main religious text in the Judeo-Christian group of traditions.
The analogous holy book of another religion or belief system.
senses.example: He conveys to his foreign students the importance of the Qur'an by explaining that it is the Bible of Islam.

senses.definition: The principal important document of some area of skill or expertise.
senses.example: This technical handbook is the Bible of our trade.

senses.definition: A specific version, edition, translation, or copy of one of the above-mentioned texts.
senses.example: He had just become able to read, with much effort, short sentences in his Bible, and was constantly engaged during his leisure hours in studying its pages.

senses.definition: A surname originating as a matronymic.
